notes.title: An Update
notes.notes:
Hey there, hope you’re all doing well! It’s been a while, hasn’t it? I’ve been busy trying out and learning different game engines to use for my next game. After trying out GameMaker2 and Unity, I eventually decided on Godot and am in the process of making a small game with it. What game you ask? A top down twin-stick shooter set in the Fuchian Chronicles universe!

https://i.imgur.com/6Q55VUN.gif

The Last Fox Fighter (working title) is still in its prototype stages and I’m still figuring out how to add the features that I want, but I’ve made good progress in the 2-3 weeks I’ve spent on it! Normally I’d list out what’s in the prototype right now here, but you can see for yourself. The prototype is publicly available on its itch.io page, and you can play it in your browser! I update the game whenever I’ve added enough new features to justify an update, and feedback is always welcome!

I should be clear however, that I haven’t decided to make the Last Fox Fighter into a full game just yet. I’m still waiting to see how a few things pan out, and will continue to work on the prototype in the meantime. Once I’m satisfied with it, I’ll release the Last Fox Fighter as a free DLC for Fuchian Chronicles. If I do decide to make it into a full game, it will serve as a demo instead.

One final thing. If you follow me on Twitter/X, you may have noticed that my account has been suspended. The stated reason was that I violated a rule, but I don’t know what rule I violated and my best guess is that it’s because I often posted links to my Steam/itchio pages which might have been flagged as bot behaviour. So far I’ve only gotten one sentence automated responses saying they won’t help whenever I tried to appeal, so at this point I’ve written off the account as lost [strike]and have made a new one: @ShenTzuGame[/strike]. Nevermind, the new account got banned as well for ban evasion. Which, while understandable, is incredibly frustrating since I only made a new account because I wasn't able to appeal my old account. I'm trying to appeal again from the new account, and so far I haven't gotten an automated response yet so maybe there's hope. I'll edit again when there's a clear outcome.

I’m considering other platforms such as Mastadon or Bluesky as well, and will let you guys know if I make accounts there. Of course, you can still reach me here in the Steam Community or email me at shentzugames@yahoo.com. 

That’s it for this time, thanks for your time. I’ll post again when I have more to share, so look forward to that!

Sincerely,
ShenTzu

notes.title: Pre-Release Update 3
notes.notes:
Hello everyone, and welcome to what should be the final update prior to Fuchian Chronicle’s full release! This will be a text heavy one so please bear with me here.

I’ve fixed all the issues I mentioned in the previous updates, and addressed another one of the major complaints that I got:

[center]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/e4c1c1_adbdddf97f3741539435a5117b7b4a58~mv2.gif[/center]

New walking animations! This was an issue that was first brought up near the start of development, and I thought I had fixed it with a sprite update. The feedback I got however, made it clear that the lackluster animation hadn’t been adequately addressed. I hope that this new update goes further towards fixing that issue.

Now I’m back to adding new content to the game and playtesting to make sure everything is in order. I’ve already showed most of the new stuff I’m adding in the previous updates, but there is one thing I’m taking out: selectable battlemodes. The main reason for this is that the Action Time Battle (ATB) mode simply looks too unpolished, especially with how barebones the enemy ATB gauges looks and how it doesn’t line up with the enemy when the camera moves. If there’s one takeaway I got from all the feedback I got, it’s that looking unpolished is a big red flag. I’m fully aware that there are other parts of Fuchian Chronicles that look unpolished, but many of those cannot be feasibly fixed at this point. I can improve polish by removing ATB mode though, and so I’m doing that, and setting Conditional Turn Based (CTB) mode as the only battle mode. I don’t know how much being able to change battle modes affects your enjoyment of Fuchian Chronicles, but I hope you can see my reasoning and thank you for understanding.

The Steam store page is in need of serious overhaul as well. All the screenshots and trailers need replacing, I’ll need to rewrite the introduction blurb and some of the descriptions, and I’m even looking into getting a brand new logo for Fuchian Chronicles. I am taking new screenshots and recording clips as I playtest (and I’m sharing them on my Twitter/X @ShenTzuGames), but I’m in the slightly awkward position where Fuchian Chronicles is purchasable and playable while the new screenshots aren’t reflective of the current published version of the game. Because of this, I’ve decided to hold off on publishing any changes to the store page until final release so anyone who buys the game now will get what was advertised. As stated before, the price will not increase upon final release, but as a matter of disclosure, Fuchian Chronicles is part of the Steam Spring Sale, which will likely have a larger discount than the launch discount. If you’d like to hold off on buying/playing Fuchian Chronicles until final release, I’d completely understand and even encourage you to do so if you’re not satisfied with what you’ve seen in my updates.

So when is final release? Barring any major set-back or unforeseen circumstances, Fuchian Chronicles will come out of Early Access on April 19th, 2024! It’s been a long road, longer than I anticipated (but that’s how things are sometimes), and I thank you for your support thus far. I’m looking forward to finishing Fuchian Chronicles, and hope you will enjoy the game!

- ShenTzu

notes.title: Pre-Release Update 2
notes.notes:
Early update announcement this time for a few reasons. First, more art!

https://i.imgur.com/zfE8SwW.png

Getting art for all party members was one of my priorities in this final phase of development, and with Ferdi and Arlette’s portraits completed, that’s that part finished! Some of their dialogues have also been updated, namely their introductions. A handful of other recurring characters may get more art later, but there are more pressing matters at the moment.

If you’ve been following my social media (@ShenTzuGames on X/Twitter), you’ll know that I recently got a lot of feedback for Fuchian Chronicles. I’m extremely grateful for this, especially since they pointed out several major issues I had not considered. Unfortunately some of them simply can’t be feasibly fixed at this stage given my limited resources, but I am committed to improving what I can, starting with updating the UI.

https://i.imgur.com/stBXcVQ.png

https://i.imgur.com/d9jpWOE.jpeg

https://i.imgur.com/9cuxcwU.png

I will readily admit that I put too much focus on looking “unique” and overlooked player readability, and I hope you will agree that the updated UI is much cleaner than before. Additional fixes are in the works, and more feedback is always welcome! That said, these fixes likely won’t be implemented until final release, so I won’t be updating the screenshots and trailers on the Steam page at this point as to not give the wrong impression. Please follow my X/Twitter if you’d like to see the updates as they come. 

Finally and perhaps most importantly, the price of Fuchian Chronicle has been permanently reduced to $7.99 USD as of this announcement. I was under the impression that a cheap game would be seen as not worth considering, and overcorrected when I gave it a price tag of over $10 USD, especially considering the other amazing games you can get at that price. Just to be clear, $7.99 USD will be the final base price at release. If you previously bought Fuchian Chronicles at a higher price, I thank you for the support! I understand if you wish to refund the game though, and hope you’ll buy it again at the reduced price if you do. Fuchian Chronicles will also be part of the upcoming RPG Maker Franchise Sale and Steam Spring Sales (I can’t say when, but really soon!), so look forward to that!

That’s it for this time. I need to travel for two weeks starting next week, and combined with the need to fix the aforementioned issues, I’m currently predicting a final release date of sometime between early to mid-April. I’ll announce a concrete release date when I know one. As always, thank you for the continued support, and I hope you enjoy Fuchian Chronicles!

- ShenTzu

notes.title: Pre-Release Update 1
notes.notes:
First update after Fuchian Chronicles’ story officially concluded! If you follow my social media (@ShenTzuGames on X/Twitter, u/ShenTzuGames on Reddit), you’ll see that I’ve been much more active in posting stuff from the game. Now that development of the game proper is winding down, I have more time for these things and making more promotional material, so look forward to those!

That’s not to say there aren’t changes to the game in the works. For starters:

https://i.imgur.com/BxQDEPD.png

Character profiles! They’re mostly done now and I will be/have been sharing them over time on my X/Twitter. Not every named character will have one, but I did make one for most recurring characters, as well as a few of the important ones. That said… you may have noticed who the profile is of: Fitz! 

I originally didn’t have much planned for Fitz, and even planned to kill him off in Chapter 2 (hint: he can still die there depending on your actions!). But he got a bigger role as a development went on, and even became a temporary party member in certain points. With that in mind, I decided it was time he finally got his own portraits for all his appearances. I’ll also be expanding his introduction in Chapter 1 where he was basically another no-face NPC, and may expand his appearances in other chapters too.

Other parts of the game are slated for tweaking as well, one of them being increasing the number of autosave/quicksave slots from 1 to 3. That’s already finished, but I haven’t uploaded the change yet because IT WILL RENDER THE FIRST FOUR (4) SLOTS INACCESSIBLE. This means that if you have any manual saves in slots 1-4, THEY WILL BE OVERWRITTEN. So if you’re in the middle of the game, please make a manual save in one of the later save slots (slot 10 or higher to be safe). The plan is to publish this change when Fuchian Chronicles comes out of Early Access, but if you guys would like, I can publish this change earlier along with what I have finished. Let me know if that’s something you’d like, and I’ll make a small post warning you guys if I push the update early.

That’s it for this update! As always, please let me know if you encounter any bugs and I’ll fix them asap. I would also like to ask for another favour: please consider writing a review for Fuchian Chronicles! It would really help with the algorithm, and I’d love to hear your thoughts on the game, both positive and negative. Thank you once again for all your support, and I hope you like my game!

- ShenTzu

notes.title: Chapter 7 Update 1
notes.notes:
Wow, it’s been a month already? Somehow it really doesn’t feel like it. Either way, it’s time for the first Chapter 7 update!

https://i.imgur.com/P1m6DLA.jpeg

Planning is complete, and I’ve gotten started on making maps for the chapter, including the one above. That is Protentum Station, a secret Galactic Fuchian Empire research facility and where the majority of Chapter 7 will take place. I can’t say too much about what’s being studied there due to spoilers, but if you’ve been paying attention in previous chapters, you might have a good idea already!

There is one more thing I’d like to bring up. As you may or may not know, Unity recently announced a new “Runtime fee”, where developers using the Unity game engine will have to pay a $0.20 fee PER INSTALL of the game if their game has made $200,000 USD or more in the last 12 months and have at least 200,000 lifetime game installs (those who pay for the Unity Pro and Unity Enterprise subscriptions have a higher threshold and lower fees). Fuchian Chronicles is fortunately unaffected as it is built using RPGMaker MV, but as a fellow indie game developer, I cannot stay quiet about this egregious move by the higher ups at Unity (who allegedly sold their shares in the company prior to the announcement). 

As this is a developing story, details may change and Unity may even walk back this new policy entirely. However, the fact remains that they have shown that they prioritize profits to the point of nickel and diming small developers, many of whom can’t afford this additional fee. Even if they completely walk back the Runtime fee, there’s no telling if they will try to push it again after the heat dies down. I had been considering switching over to using Unity for my future games after finishing Fuchian Chronicles, but now I’ll be looking elsewhere unless there are drastic changes in Unity policy and leadership.

Thank you for taking the time to read my little rant, I felt it was my responsibility to spread awareness of the issue where I can. That’s it for this update, I’ll see you all next time.

Cheers,
ShenTzu

notes.title: Chapter 6 Progress Update 3
notes.notes:
Another month, another update! I’m working on the script still, but in the meantime, here’s a new character!

https://i.imgur.com/9e94cVV.jpeg

Her name is Fuchs (as in Fuchian), and if you’ve played the original game, Space Fox Kimi, you’ll know her as Kimi’s party member and GFE’s envoy to Earth in that game. Obviously she has much less screentime now and her role is different, but I liked her character in the past and wanted to give her a minor role at least.

Finally, a little bit of bad news: I’m afraid that the script is taking longer than I would like, mainly because of a newly discovered narrative plothole that needed me to revise certain events in chapter 6. I hope to finish by the end of July, but I’m not entirely confident about that deadline. I will commit to finishing the chapter by mid-August though, so it won’t be delayed further. Thank you for understanding.

That’s it for this time! Barring any critical hotfixes or real life emergencies, the next announcement will be the release of chapter 6. See you then!

- ShenTzu

notes.title: Chapter 6 Progress Update 2
notes.notes:
Has it been another month already? Time sure is going faster than I anticipated… Well, time for another updated! This one's a little early, but I didn't want to sit on this particular update for reasons that'll be apparent.

The new maps are finished, though if time allows I’d like to expand on one of the areas. For now I’m working on the script, which is where the bulk of the work will be for this chapter. There’s a lot going on following the events of Chapter 5! Speaking of which...

https://i.imgur.com/U2bpLen.png

Chapter 6 will have the first meaningful interactions with the bunnoids… and a bunnoid party member! I won’t reveal the circumstances of her joining since it’s a major plot point, but I hope you look forward to it!

Finally, a small update with pretty a pretty big impact: a difficulty setting! I originally designed the game to avoid having overly simple combat that can be won by spamming the regular attack, but now I realize I may have gone too far and made the game frustratingly hard at places. My apologies for that. There is now a difficulty setting in the options menu that ranges from “Story Mode” for players who want to focus on enjoying the story, and “Challenge” difficulty for those who like… well, a challenge. Please be warned that the “Challenge” difficulty may not be balanced, and may even make some encounters outright impossible. You can change the difficulty at any time, so if you do get stuck feel free to lower the difficulty to get past those encounters. This update is now live for both the base game and the demo as of this announcement. Speaking of which, now would be a good time to play the demo if you haven’t already (hint hint). It contains a side story that doesn’t show up in the main game after all! I don't think it would and didn't find any issues while testing, but if this update broke anything please let me know and I'll fix it asap.

That’s it for this update! At this point I’m a little hesitant to promise that Chapter 6 will be released in a month, but I’ll certainly do my best to meet this goal. Either way, you can look forward to another announcement then, and more frequent updates on my Twitter @ShenTzuGames! Thank you as always for your continued support!

- ShenTzu

notes.title: Chapter 6 Progress Update 1
notes.notes:
Another month, another update, hope everyone’s doing well! Some unexpected business took me away from work for a wwhile, but I was able finish planning out Chapter 6. I can’t share much about it because spoilers, but I do have this for you!
https://i.imgur.com/MviSvy2.jpeg
If the setting looks familiar, it should! Chapter 6 goes back to where it all began, Z-7421, or as the bunnoids call it, Sotenye! After the events of Chapter 5, the GFE can finally properly communicate with the bunnoids and learn more about the enemy they’ve been fighting for so long, and maybe even broker a ceasefire. Perhaps with understanding, there can finally be peace?

That’s it for this update! I understand it’s a short one, but I haven’t had the time to work on that much on the game this past month. I promise the next update will have more, especially in the graphics department. Until then, thank you for your continued support! 

- ShenTzu

notes.title: Chapter 4 Progress Update 2
notes.notes:
Month two of developing Chapter 4! All the new maps have been finished, and so I’ve moved onto writing the script. 

https://i.imgur.com/XyB1ovt.gif

And that’s it! See you next time!

…I jest, but the truth is I’ve had to take on a few side jobs to help pay the bills, so progress this month has been slower than I would like (did you know I did the maps for Sierra Lee’s Once Ever After, and a few maps for her other game, The Last Sovereign?). At this point I can’t say for sure if this will lead to a delay to the planned release of Chapter 4 in a month or so, but wanted to give you guys a heads up in case there is. I’d also like to take this opportunity to reassure you guys that I will finish the game even if I need to take a full time job to pay bills, though if it does come to that, each chapter will likely take much longer to release.

Now that’s out of the way, let’s get back to Chapter 4.

Right now I don’t plan on adding any new major features/mechanics for this chapter, mainly to reduce the odds of additional delays. There will still be new items, enemies, and equipment of course, just no new brand new mechanics like how I added weapon proficiency and equipment modding in Chapter 3. I do have a few other ideas I’d like to implement, but those are mainly on the backburner… except one.

The Demo!

I know the importance of demos for games, but decided against making one since I felt it was unfair to have one while only one or two chapters were released as paid content. This is why I’m only making a demo once Chapter 4 is released. Yes, making a demo, as in it’ll be new content. I already roughly mapped out how it’ll go and just need to work out a few kinks and plot consistencies to make sure it ties in well with established events. Based on my plans, it probably won’t be as long as a full chapter, but should fill in a bit of the story that I couldn’t fit in before.

That’s it for this update! Hope you look forward to the release!

- ShenTzu

notes.title: Minor Update - New Savings Features and Fixed Playtime Tracking
notes.notes:
-	Updated saving system. Autosaves now have a dedicated save slot which cannot be manually saved into, thanks to CloudyCloudcloud for the suggestion! While I was at it, I also added quicksaving/quickloading to the game (which also comes with its own dedicated save slot). Press F5 to quicksave and F9 to quickload. Of course, you still won’t be able to quicksave/load when saving/loading is disabled.
-	Fixed playtime tracking. Apparently the way playtime was being tracked was dependent on your computer/monitor’s FPS, meaning that you could have a drastically different playtime than reality. That’s been fixed now, and the playtime should reflect real time. Don’t worry if you see play time as “Na : Na : Na”, it’ll go back to normal when you next make a save. It does reset the time to “00 : 00 : 00” though, thank you for understanding. There’s also an option in the debug menu to reset the playtime in case the timer does not fix itself, or if you want to reset it for any reason. Thanks to Screethegargoyle for catching this!
-	Did you know that taking a shower (either at home or in the crew bathrooms) actually gives you a minor buff to agility and evasion for the chapter? Well now you do! And now when you take a shower, you’ll be notified about the buff.
-	Fixed a few instances where the incorrect portrait was shown in Chapter 3.

Follow me on Twitter @ShenTzuGames for more frequent updates, and as always, thank you for playing my game and for helping me with bug reporting and suggestions! I hope you enjoyed the game so far, and hope you’ll look forward to Chapter 4!

notes.title: Chapter 3 Update 3
notes.notes:
Just a quick update this time, though with some important news. 

The good news is, Chapter 3 is finished! I’m just waiting on some art, and while I’m doing that I’m adding a few more features to the game. Which brings me to the other bit of news.

Thus far I’ve tried my best to add fixes to get around the need to restart the game when new features are added, but unfortunately there’s finally a new feature that I’d like to add that is incompatible with existing saves. That feature is weapon proficiency, making the character more effective using a type of weapon the more they use it. I’ve been trying to find ways to add more incentive to fighting, and think this would be a good way to do so in addition to the other stuff. 

https://i.imgur.com/n3NJFmV.png

As mentioned before, this new feature unfortunately does require a new save. I thank you for understanding, and will try to add something to make it easier for players who have already played before to get back to where they left off. I’ll also try my best to avoid adding features that require restarts, but can’t promise that it won’t happen again, especially if the new feature would significantly improve the game.

On the bright side, you’ll be able to see the changes in the cutscenes that resulted from the new portrait system, so I hope you’ll enjoy that.

And since there will be a restart, I’m taking the opportunity to add additional features. I won’t reveal what those features are just yet, mainly because I’m still testing them. Based on the current state of things, I’m estimating that Chapter 3, along with all the new features, will be released at the end of July. Look forward to it!

notes.title: Chapter 3 Progress Update 2
notes.notes:
Has it been another month already? Geez times goes by so fast. Time for another update!

The maps and script for Chapter 3 are finished, all that’s left is to add the events in and test things! Before I can do that however, I need rework a lot of the cutscenes and interactions in Chapters 1 and 2. Why? Because I’m making the portraits/busts much more dynamic!
[previewyoutube=EQO4qMlea7Q;full][/previewyoutube]
As you can see, portraits can now alongside each other, and can also move to better convey the action taking place. I was debating about whether to implement this now, or focus on releasing Chapter 3 first, but ultimately decided that it was better to do this now since the longer I wait to add this feature, the more I would have to redo. Hopefully this won’t delay Chapter 3’s release too much, but if there are any delays, I thank you for your understanding and hope you will agree that this addition is worth it.

I mentioned in my previous progress update that I was adding/reworking other features as well. In addition to the Databank, another important feature that’s being updated is the crafting menu. You will be able to craft multiple items at once, and will no longer be kicked out of the menu after crafting a single item. More importantly, you will also be able to disassemble items into raw materials!

https://i.imgur.com/WIxfFxh.png

Considering the item used in crafting is called the “Reassembler”, it didn’t make much sense to not be able to break down unwanted items into more useful materials. But now you can! You will be able to disassemble just about any consumable, and even some trophies, in a pinch.

As always, follow me on Twitter @ShenTzuGames for more frequent updates. If everything goes according to plan, this should be the last progress update before the release of Chapter 3. Either way, I’ll make another post in about a month. See you then!

- ShenTzu

notes.title: Chapter 3 Progress Update
notes.notes:
Hello everyone! It’s been about a month since the release of Chapter 2, and so it’s time for a little update on my progress on Chapter 3.

https://i.imgur.com/3Zv5RcD.jpeg

Thus far the only space based content has been individual battles, but Chapter 3 will introduce the first real space based map! Considering space based exploration is one of the marketed selling points of the game, I’m happy to finally introduce some space exploration. While ground based maps will still be the focus, I plan on having more space maps later on. 

Of course, Chapter 3 will still have ground content.

https://i.imgur.com/K74J4af.jpeg

Chapter 3 will also have the first look at a bunnoid locale. It’ll be the first real chance to learn a bit about the bunnoids and their culture, who have so far been more or less a faceless enemy. What are the bunnoids like? Are they really all machines? Do they all eat carrots? You will finally be able to start answering some of these questions, though the answer to the last one is almost certainly yes.

And finally, I’ve been gradually adding new features and improving on some existing features in the game. One of the major new additions to the game is… the Databank!

https://i.imgur.com/UB0lUPC.png

The journal system I’ve been using, though functional, is rather inelegant and limited. Now there will be a proper in-game encyclopedia, recording enemies, equipment, lore, and more! More encyclopedia entries will be added as the game progresses, and I may add additional categories (such as character profiles) later on. I’m working on other features as well, but I’ll save them for a future blog post.

One last thing: Thank you thus far for the support, including catching bugs I missed and giving suggestions! I posted in the suggestions thread earlier but would like to re-iterate: if you agree with someone else’s suggestion, especially regarding game difficulty, please say so! It would really help me gauge which suggestions would help improve the game the most. 

Once again, thank you for playing my game, and I hope you look forward to Chapter 3!

- ShenTzu
